summary: American Nazi Party teen Frank Sweeney spent six decades in and out of prison: a botched bank robbery, a shootout with police, Rhodesian mercenary service, mail fraud, false leads in a Soviet spy manhunt, and years of racist stalking by postcard in Idaho.

evidence.note: Robert introduces a two-part Weird Little Guys episode by Molly Conger, a network show
1962 toy-gun bank robbery attempt to fund the American Nazi Party opens the story
1967 machine-gun standoff with police; convicted of attempted homicide
Background on Rhodesian UDI and the Bush War as a white-minority civil conflict
Service as a foreign recruit in the Rhodesian Light Infantry, claims of executing prisoners
Mail fraud selling imaginary submachine guns under a forged alias
Christopher Boyce, TRW, CIA cables and the Whitlam affair
Letters mailed from South Africa plant false leads in the Boyce manhunt
Jailhouse informant against Joseph Paul Franklin, then expelled from witness protection
1990s consulting business advising first-time federal prisoners
Racist, slur-laden postcard harassment campaign against an Idaho family
Sentenced for stalking in December 2019, released 2022; brief coda only

notes: Crossover: Molly Conger's Weird Little Guys episode on Frank Sweeney. Roles and time filled anyway. Primary theme is a judgement call between policing-incarceration (prisons, informant deals, witness protection, prison consulting) and fraud-grift. Covered span starts at the 1962 robbery; birth and childhood are brief mentions. NJ and ID both central, so no subdivision. Boyce and Franklin birth/death years from general knowledge.
